name: NAIRA NIWAS · one building, one window a post
one_line: The season told as one blush Bombay-Deco building, Naira Niwas, three bays wide and four storeys tall: every post is a reel or a moving carousel that finds its window in the building, opens it and lights it on one witty, true moment of Indian building life, and the twelve covers, posted in order, assemble on the profile into the building itself, lit from the shops at street level to a wedding on the terrace.
big_idea:
Every woman this feed is for has stood on her balcony on Diwali night and looked across at the building opposite: a kandil in every window, a different light in every flat, somebody's lamps on the ledge, somebody's curtain drawn. NAIRA NIWAS is that building. It is drawn in Naira blush in the Bombay-Deco manner of Dadar, Matunga, Shivaji Park and Marine Drive (speed-line pilasters, eyebrow sunshades, sunburst grills, a stepped corner tower with the name on it), three bays wide and four storeys tall: shops at street level, two floors of flats, a terrace on top. Twelve bays, twelve posts, the exact shape of the 3 x 4 profile grid.

Each post opens one bay and lights it. The Naira shop's shutter goes up on a tent card that says BACK IN 5 MINUTES (it was eleven weeks). The bangle shop is busy the night before Karwa Chauth and the cuff needs no soap. Four blush boxes wait at the watchman's desk and he isn't telling who they are for. In 103 the window seat is still disputed. In 102 the brass gets its tamarind and lemon. On 101's balcony the panatis burn down and a line of stones stays lit. In 203 she said 'kahi nako' and he believed her. In 202 a chit asks to borrow one of two necklaces. By the lift a notice says LOST: ONE EARRING. On the terrace the cousins have rehearsed for three weeks, the moon comes back with nobody fasting, and on the last Sunday the whole building gets its wedding lights.

The motion is the idea, not decoration. Every reel opens on the whole building at exactly one third scale, which is the profile grid itself: the season so far is lit, the coming weeks are dark windows with unlit kandils. The camera finds this week's window, the window opens, the light comes on, the real piece catches it, one line lands, and the camera pulls back to a building with one more window lit. Followers watch it fill up for four weeks; a visitor to the profile sees it finished. On the grid the covers are not a puzzle: each tile is a whole bay and a complete picture in the home feed, but every bay shares the same pilasters, string courses and the same blush kandil hung in the same place, so posted in order they become one building.

The emblem is the Naira kandil: an akash kandil in Naira blush with the I-flower cut out of its face, hung under the eyebrow of every bay at the same spot. In Maharashtra the kandil goes up before Diwali and stays up through Kartik, to Tripurari Purnima on 24 Nov, so it is true in every post from 27 Oct to 22 Nov. When it turns in the evening air it throws the Naira flower across the plaster, one full turn every ten seconds, the owner's own number for the flower.

The building is drawn; the life inside it is photographed. Every piece is its own listing photograph, cut out, at true relative scale beside its one real prop (a panati, a brass vati, a soap dish, a Naira box). The wit comes from the life the buyer actually lives in a housing society, which none of the four proposals and almost no Indian brand has used: the watchman, the notice by the lift, the neighbour with your spare key, the borrowed necklace, the window seat, the bangle-wala's soap, 'kahi nako'. A stranger names it in three seconds: a building at Diwali, and every post lights one window.
why_better_than_A_and_B:
AGAINST OPTION A, NAIRA MATCHING CENTRE (245/300, the chosen A). A is the truest and most commercial plan, but it is a stills feed: 4 statics, 6 carousels, 2 reels, so on a profile the owner wants to move, ten tiles never do. In V3 every one of the twelve moves, and the movement is each post's mechanism (a shutter rises, a curtain draws, lamps burn down, a lift gate concertinas, earrings sway), never a light sweep added to a still. A's grid is a twelve-shade colour rhythm with a tag that the selection had to pin to one corner; V3's grid is a picture: the twelve covers assemble into one lit building, and every reel opens on that building at one third scale, so the reels literally preview the profile. A spends its wit on one institution (the matching counter) and needs a WhatsApp matching service the studio must staff; V3's wit comes from twelve different, specific moments of society life and needs no new service. Commercially V3 keeps A's best moves (the gift guide on 1 Nov, the Bhaubeej piece 8 days early, a three-piece set on the top-left tile, the BUY line on the set and gift posts) and adds what A lacks: a piece on every one of the twelve tiles (A's tulsi tile needed one grafted in), packaging as a recurring object (the real Naira box on P3 and P7; unboxing is this account's biggest topic, 3,410 likes), and a price card at the end of every reel. Where both use the kandil, A's is one Diwali joke; V3's is the emblem on all twelve covers and the source of the feed's one patterned light, the Naira flower.

AGAINST OPTION B, MANGAL (225/300, the chosen B). B is the funniest and the most PTAT-like, and its weakness is density and build risk: nine scripts that each need a native reader, a seal plus wordmark plus eyebrow plus price stack on ten tiles, about a dozen bespoke domestic drawings, and Mummy's-house nostalgia (almirah, ₹501 lifafa, missed call) that the reference judge called common in Indian D2C. V3 keeps B's energy (an Indian vernacular world, drawn frames around real photographs, a recurring emblem, a named place with a cast) but runs on one drawing (the building, built once, with twelve states), one Devanagari word on four tiles, and a strict per-tile budget: one opening, one prop, one piece, one line, the kandil and the plate. Its humour is present-day and specific to the 35-54 woman who lives in a housing society now, not her childhood, so it is newer ground than B's and no competitor has claimed it.

AGAINST BOTH. It is the only plan in which the profile itself is the payoff (posted in order, the grid becomes the building; the reels show it filling up), the only one built motion-first at the owner's own tempo (the kandil turns once every 10 s, the box drawer opens in the site's own 1.1 s, nothing faster than a calm camera move), the only one whose emblem sits in the same place on all twelve covers and is true for the whole run (Kartik kandils stay up to 24 Nov), and the only one that does not open Karwa Chauth on the moon (A, B and the other V3 all do; V3 goes to the bangle shop). Its finale moves to the emerald-green set (necklace 20, bracelet 16, huggies 15 in stock) while A and B both close on ruby, which by 22 Nov may be down to single digits at the current one-a-day pace. It is also the most buildable motion system of the lot: one HTML world, twelve bay components with states, seven reusable moves, 18 AI layer plates (no jewellery, no faces, no text) and three new cut-outs.
why_it_fits:
BRAND. Naira calls itself 'a couture house first' and 'a house that sews'; Naira Niwas is that house made literal, a building with the brand's name on its crown, painted in the brand's own blush (the colour of the Naira box), with the brand's own flower turning in every window at the owner's own 10-second pace. It uses only the house kit: the real wordmark (on the crown and on every end card, nowhere else, so never twice in a frame), the I-flower (as the kandil's cut-out and its light, inside the 6-15% ghost rule), Velista caps with a lowercase Cormorant turn, Jost labels with Poppins for the rupee, sharp corners, gold hairlines, the real blush box from the site's own 3D scene, and only palette families the brand already owns (identity blush, Red Room, the Lilac / Sage / Apricot editions, exhibition bottle green, Lac).

BUYER. Women 35-54 placed 64 of 100 attributed purchases; 46% of orders ship to Maharashtra, mostly Mumbai and Nashik, where she lives in a housing society. Everything in the feed is her life this month: the bangle shop on Karwa Chauth eve, the watchman taking in Diwali parcels, Bhaubeej, Diwali Padwa (a Maharashtrian buying muhurat), brass polished with tamarind and lemon, panatis on the balcony ledge, the akash kandil, the society notice by the lift, the terrace sangeet, the wedding lights on the building. Gifting and self-purchase both run through it (the gate is a gift guide; 'kahi nako' is a self-purchase).

DATA. The formula that sells is one real piece + one everyday Indian object + one witty Indian line + one exact fact ('Anaar, pre-peeled.', ₹335 a purchase, ROAS 4.52): every bay is exactly that, with the object as the bay's one prop. Ruby is the hero stone (8 of 13 bracelets since 16 Oct) and opens the season; Edition Two had the account's best week (34 purchases at ₹854) and supplies eight of the twelve heroes; the four bestsellers by units and revenue (Woven Gold Hoops, Prism Rivière, Baguette Tennis Bracelet, Heartbead) all appear, plus deep, unsold stock that content can move (Silk Mesh Cuff 40/0 sold, Kiss Knot 40/0, Baguette Tennis Necklace 70/0, Marquise Layering Set 40/1). 69% of orders are one piece, so seven posts carry a basket (four gifts, a set of two, the 'wear both' metals, four huggie colours, a three-piece set). Sunday noon and Fri/Tue 18:30-19:00 are the order peaks and carry the posts. The grid has been silent for 76 days, so P1 owns the silence.

OWNER TASTE. Indian everyday-object wit with restraint and love (no one mocked: the watchman, the bangle-wala and the neighbours are the heroes of their jokes); lilac and purple (lilac-mast window, amethyst huggies, a plum and aubergine night); moody night grounds without black; clean plates (one prop, one piece, lots of plaster); exact facts and honest corrections (the cuff's 2.5 cm opening, 'listed as tarnish free', shell pearls kept out of the shower, emerald-green not emerald); and motion at her own numbers, slow and continuous, never jittery, no lyrics. Nothing she has rejected appears: no black, sand or beige grounds, no stuck-on florals, no sticker or stamp soup, no faces, no spice props, no soap papdi, no grand copy, no offer on any image.
motion_language:
HOUSE PACE. The slowest thing on screen sets the tempo: in every bay the kandil turns through one full torsion every 10.0 s (the owner's number for the flower) and sways ±1.2° on its thread every 6.4 s. Camera moves 1.8-2.0 s; openings 1.0-2.2 s (the Naira box drawer opens in 1.1 s and closes in 1.0 s, the site's own REVEAL figures); lights-on 0.8-1.2 s; type 0.6 s. No shot shorter than 1.5 s, every headline held at least 2.0 s, reels 14-18 s, carousel video slides 6-12 s. Nothing fast, nothing jittery, no flash frames, no camera shake.

EASING. Entrances (type, glows, sparkles): cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), the site's reveal curve, type rising 16 px from opacity 0. Camera and every opening (shutter, shutters, doors, curtain, drawer, lift gate): cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1). Constant motion (kandil torsion and sway, fan shadow, flame breathing, earring sway, cloud drift): sinusoidal. No bounce, no spring, no overshoot, nothing from scale 0 (start at 0.96 and opacity 0).

THE SEVEN MOVES, the whole vocabulary. (1) ESTABLISHING: C-WORLD at scale 0.331492 fills the 1080 x 1920 frame, which makes it the profile grid; posted bays lit, this bay's kandil lights first (0.5 s), coming bays dark with unlit kandils; the sky is the week's (dusk, Diwali night, night, wedding night). (2) THE FIND: zoom to this bay at scale 1.0 in 1.8 s, tracking the bay's centre so it grows in place (formula in C-WORLD). (3) THE OPENING, one per storey: GROUND, a rolling shutter rises into its drum (2.2 s) or the gate leaves fold back; FIRST FLOOR, louvred shutters or glazed doors swing on their hinges (rotateY, perspective 1600 px, 1.2 s); SECOND FLOOR, a voile curtain draws aside (1.6 s) or a brass lift gate concertinas (2.0 s); TERRACE, string lights come on bulb by bulb (70 ms stagger). (4) LIGHTS ON: the room warms from its dusk value to its lit value with a soft radial bloom from its source and warm spill on the plaster around the opening (0.8-1.2 s). (5) THE GLINT: one light sweep across the piece, masked to its alpha (a 120 px band, 55% peak, screen, 1.1 s), with at most three four-point sparkles (the site's sparkle path) on the brightest stones; once per post, except where light is the joke (P6). (6) THE PULL-BACK: back to the establishing scale in 2.0 s, the bay now lit and its kandil glowing. (7) THE PLATE: the end card (C-ENDCARD), the NAIRA wordmark on a brass plate with its flower turning on the I's stem at 36° a second.

LOOP LOGIC. Reels: the end card holds 2.6 s and its last 0.5 s dissolves into frame 0, so the reel loops into its own beginning. Carousel video slides: frame 0 is the cover and the last frame returns exactly to it; whatever moves on slide 1 is cyclical (sway, sweep, drift, flutter, breathing, a drawer that opens and closes); whatever changes state (a polish wipe, a moonrise) lives on slide 2 or later.

WHAT NEVER MOVES. The jewellery's form: never warped, mirrored, recoloured, spun or scaled on its own (the camera scales it; it may ride a drawer, rise up to 24 px, or hang and swing as a real earring does). The wordmark's letters (only its flower turns, on its stem, as on the site). Prices, facts and plates (they fade in and hold). The building's geometry (no wobble, no bend, no squash). Type never types on, bounces, scales or tracks.

LIGHT. Warm only: interiors at a 2700 K look, glints ivory #FFF7E6 on gold tone and neutral #F4F2F0 on rhodium; the kandil's flower is the only patterned light; no lens flares, no confetti, no fireworks, no fake bokeh.

DEPTH. Inside a bay only: foreground architecture (shutters, frames, railings, curtain) moves 1.15x the interior during camera moves; far things in a room (a shelf, a notice board, a bangle wall) carry 1-2 px blur; every cut-out gets a contact shadow (radial ellipse, multiply 30-38%) plus the kit's .cut shadows.

SOUND. One instrumental per reel from Meta's Sound Collection, no lyrics, no vocals, added in-app; under it an original foley track baked into the MP4: the same 1.2 s building ambience on every establishing shot (evening birds, a far scooter, the hum of a street) and 2-4 timed effects per reel (listed per post). Music ducks 4 dB under foley. Carousel video slides are silent.

In the grid it is 50 x 150 px: a pink lantern top-left of every tile, the repeating mark the way PTAT's MILNI lockup repeats; it is never placed beside the wordmark (end cards carry no kandil).

Each bay is a component with three states: CLOSED (shutters down, shutters shut, curtain drawn, gate shut, no interior light, kandil unlit), OPENING (its post's animation) and LIT (open, interior lit, kandil lit). Bay origins: r1c1 P12 (0,0) · r1c2 P11 (1089,0) · r1c3 P10 (2178,0) · r2c1 P9 (0,1449) · r2c2 P8 (1089,1449) · r2c3 P7 (2178,1449) · r3c1 P6 (0,2898) · r3c2 P5 (1089,2898) · r3c3 P4 (2178,2898) · r4c1 P3 (0,4347) · r4c2 P2 (1089,4347) · r4c3 P1 (2178,4347). Camera: wrapper with transform-origin 0 0; establishing transform translate(0, 0.82px) scale(0.331492) (the building exactly fills 1080 x 1920); zoom to a bay with focal point P = bay origin + (540, 720): s(e) = 0.331492 x (1/0.331492)^e, F(e) = lerp(P x 0.331492 + (0, 0.82), (540, 960) on reels or (540, 720) on carousels, e), transform = translate(F - s x P) scale(s), e = cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) of time; run it in window.atTime(ms), which FEED/tools/reel.cjs calls every frame. Carousel video slides render with a copy of reel.cjs whose viewport is 1080 x 1440 (loop.cjs).
2 THE ESTABLISHING FRAME = the profile grid, in every reel. 3 THE FIND and THE PULL-BACK. 4 ONE OPENING PER STOREY (rolling shutter or gate; swinging shutters or glazed doors; voile curtain or lift gate; string lights). 5 LIGHTS ON. 6 THE GLINT. 7 THE PLATE and THE END CARD.
8 THE SCALE RULE: the building is a drawing and frames each picture like a picture frame; it is never a size reference. Inside a window everything photographed (the piece and its one prop) keeps true relative size at a stated set scale (5-14 px per mm, given per post), so a panati is the size of a panati beside the bracelet; room-sized things (a counter, a cushion, a dressing table) appear only as close surfaces cropped by the window, and far things (a shelf, a notice board, a bangle wall) are smaller and slightly soft, as depth makes them.
9 THE NAIRA BOX: the real blush drawer box, rendered from the site's own three.js scene (/home/user/naira-scroll-3790bf3e/src/lib/nairaBox: card #D9BAB3, rim #E8D2CB, black velvet bed #141112, drawer travel REVEAL.slide 0.62 units) at the angles needed, always shown drawer-end or three-quarter with the lid print out of view; it appears on P3 (four boxes at the gate) and P7 (on the sill). Fallback: an SVG built from the same proportions (square lid, depth a little under half the width).
10 THE RESIDENTS: the flats keep their people across posts without ever showing a face, so the grid has a memory. 101 is Aai (her gift waits at the gate on P3; her lamps on P6). 103 are the siblings (window seat P4; the lost earring on P9 is theirs). 202 is the friend from the evening walk (her gift on P3; her two necklaces on P8). 203 is the neighbour with your spare key (her gift on P3; 'kahi nako' on P7; her chit on P8). Captions name them; images show only their things (reading glasses, a chit, a chalk line).
11 THE SKY CLOCK: the establishing sky moves dusk (week 1) to Diwali night (week 2) to night (week 3) to a wedding night with an almost-full moon (week 4; Kartik Purnima is 24 Nov, so the moon really is almost full on 20-22 Nov).

posts.concept: After 76 silent days the grid comes back the way every Indian shop comes back. The reel opens on the whole of Naira Niwas at dusk, twelve dark bays and twelve unlit kandils, which is the exact shape of the profile grid. The camera finds the shop on the ground floor; its sage shutter rolls up into the drum; the tube light blinks twice and settles; and on the counter, standing on a blush velvet tray, is the oldest tent card in Indian retail, BACK IN 5 MINUTES, with the ruby Baguette Tennis Bracelet lying in front of it. The turn owns the gap honestly: 'eleven weeks, actually. new stock came in.' (Edition Two came in on 16 Oct.) The camera pulls back to a building with one window lit, and the season has its rule: one window a post.

posts.caption:
Back in five minutes, said the card on the counter. It was eleven weeks. New stock came in.

When the music starts the card swings on the beat. 'THREE WEEKS / OF REHEARSALS.' / 'the drops know the steps.'

posts.why: The top-left tile is what every visitor from an ad sees from 22 Nov through the December muhurats (2-6 and 11-12 Dec), so it carries the brand's name (the real wordmark, on the crown) and the season's biggest basket: the three-piece set, the BUY3 order (₹5,198 at list) that single-piece economics need. The Baguette Tennis Necklace has 70 in stock and has never sold; the set already sells as a pair (bracelet with huggies). Emerald-green rather than ruby because Ruby bracelet and huggies are at 12 and selling about one a day (and A and B both end on ruby), while green over-indexes among competitor bestsellers (1.5-1.7x) and reads beautifully against blush. The reel is the payoff of the whole system: the building dresses up and the camera pulls back to the finished grid. Sunday noon, the strongest order slot, the morning after the first muhurat.
posts.claims_check: Prices and Emerald variant stock from roster.json (25 Oct): necklace ₹2,300 (20), bracelet ₹1,699 (16), huggies ₹1,199 (15). '36 cm' from the necklace's own alt text ('worn at the base of the neck, 36 cm at true size'); bracelet and huggies words from their listings; colour always 'emerald-green cubic zirconia' (the brand's 'EMERALD GREEN, not emerald'), never 'emerald' alone. 'made to stay gold.' on gold-tone pieces, caption only. 'Free insured shipping' and 'Cash on delivery available' SAFE. No water, tarnish or allergy claim. No total with a discount, no offer on the image. The real wordmark appears once on the cover (the crown) and once on the end card, never in the same frame. निवास checked by a Marathi reader.

risks: Ruby stock: P1's Ruby bracelet is at 12 and sells about one a day. Re-read it the evening before 27 Oct; at 9 or fewer post P1 in Crystal (29; cutouts/baguette-tennis-bracelet/00-trim.png) and change the end card. Never post a piece at 5 or fewer. The finale uses the emerald-green set (20/16/15) precisely so it does not depend on ruby; re-check all three variants on 21 Nov.

Thin variants: P4's Droplet Open Cuff holds 10 Gold and 10 Silver. If Gold is under 10 on 2 Nov, P4 posts the Silver (rhodium) cuff (cutouts/droplet-open-cuff/01-trim.png) with the turn unchanged; at 5 or fewer in both it is replaced by the Silk Mesh Cuff's other metal. Silk Mesh Cuff (P2) and Kiss Knot Bangle (P7) hold 20 per metal; Mint Pear Drops (P10) 20; Baroque Shell (P11) 23. Re-read every hero the evening before its post.

The scale rule must hold in production: a doll's-house building framing life-size jewellery is a convention, not a claim, but inside each window the piece and its prop must be at true relative size (set scales given per post). Any frame where a piece reads larger than life beside a real object gets 'shown larger.' in Jost or is re-scaled. No room-sized object is ever drawn whole next to a piece.

Owner calls on brand rules: (a) the kandil carries the I-flower as a cut-out and throws it as light on all twelve covers; it is a ghost (14%) and never beside the wordmark, but it is the flower in a new role. Fallback: a four-petal jaali cut with the same motion. (b) The building's name is set in Velista ('NAIRA NIWAS') on plates and boards; the real wordmark is only on the crown and end cards. If she reads typed NAIRA as a fake logo, the plates drop line 1 and the boards carry the kit wordmark instead (then P1's and P3's reels must crop out the crown). (c) The kandil is an Indian cue on every tile, so tiles with a second cue (P6 panatis, P2 bangle wall) carry two; the paid never-list's one-cue rule is a paid rule, flagged here openly.

Native readers: बांगड्या (P2), शुभ दीपावली (P6), काही नको. (P7) and निवास (P12) are each checked on the rendered frame by a Marathi reader before posting. Any that cannot be checked is replaced, never transliterated in Velista: BANGLES on P2's board; P6 drops its Devanagari line; P7's middle beat becomes 'NOTHING,' SHE SAID. in Velista; P12's crown keeps NAIRA and NIWAS only.

Cut-outs needed: CUT-V3-01 Marquise Layering Set (the existing 00 kept the plaster plinth; recut from assets/shopify/marquise-layering-set/01.jpg and hand-check the 1.2 mm chains on bottle green), CUT-V3-02 Mint Pear Drop Earrings split into two single earrings from cutouts/mint-pear-drop-earrings/00-trim.png, each turned upright by a fixed rotation (no reshaping), CUT-V3-03 Brushed Gold Huggies at higher resolution from assets/shopify/brushed-gold-huggies/02.jpg (the existing trim is 370 px). Fine chains and braids can hold cream ground in their gaps: check every cut-out on its dark ground.

The Naira box: render it from the site's own three.js scene (headless Chromium needs WebGL via SwiftShader); confirm the blush drawer box with the black velvet bed is what customers receive today (three box looks exist in the archive). Measure a real box before render so P3 and P7 keep true scale. Never show the lid print in a frame that carries another NAIRA mark.

AI plates (18, layers only, no jewellery, faces or text): anything that reads AI-made (the dressing table, the dupattas, the panatis) falls back to flat SVG in the same colours; newsprint and the ledger must come out blank (regenerate or paint over any hallucinated letters). Budget about 20 Higgsfield credits (2 nano_banana_pro skies at about 2 each, 16 gpt_image_2_5 plates at about 1); the options together have ~66.

Motion build time: one world, twelve bays, six reels and six carousels with 14 video slides is a heavy render (about 30 fps x 16 s x 6 reels + loops). Build C-WORLD and C-KANDIL first, prove P1 end to end, then the rest reuse it. reel.cjs is fixed at 1080 x 1920; carousel loops need its 1080 x 1440 twin.

Copy truths to hold: 'eleven weeks' (last post 9-10 Aug, first 27 Oct) and 'new stock came in' (Edition Two created 16 Oct) are true; the Silk Mesh Cuff's 2.5 cm opening, 6 cm inner width and 15 mm mesh, the Droplet cuff's 'small gap', the huggies' 'hinged snap', the Marquise set's 40 cm chain and Y-lariat, and the Baroque Shell's care line are all quoted from the listings. The Toggle and Bold Nocturne Bracelet are not used (their listings and photos disagree). Baguette Huggies' hinge is in the listing text; if no listing photo shows it, P9's slide 3 says 'hinged snap closure, as listed' rather than describing the click.

Cultural tone: every joke is affectionate and true to a society (watchman, bangle-wala, neighbours, husbands on Padwa, the cousin who runs rehearsals); none mocks tailors or aunties. 'Nobody's fasting this time' (P11) touches Karwa Chauth lightly; if the owner prefers, the turn becomes 'this time it's for the guests.'

Timing: P2 posts on Karwa Chauth eve and P7 on Padwa itself, so neither promises delivery by the day (captions never do); the gift posts that need delivery (P3 on 1 Nov, P4 on 3 Nov) go out 7-10 days early. Reels are where this account bought reach, not baskets (paid reels ROAS 0.49 against feed 1.15), so every reel ends on a price card and every carousel on an index, and the BUY line runs in seven captions.
Same opener as A and B: all three options open on the Ruby Baguette Tennis Bracelet (the data says so). V3's difference is the frame and the finale (emerald-green set).

The terrace ledge (y 800-1010) is a stage drawn seen from just above on an otherwise front-on facade, the same convention as the window sills and P6's balcony ledge. The still lifes on it (P11's bracelet, P12's set) must keep their contact shadows on the ledge and never sit against the sky; if a frame reads as floating, the piece is scaled down, never warped.
